title: Balloons in hot water (বেলুন গরম পানিতে)
placement: Book page 175, the "নিজে করো" box at the end of topic 6.3.3 (two balloons, one of water and one of air, kept in hot water).
description: Interactive 3D figure for the 'নিজে করো' (do it yourself) box on page 175, the end of textbook topic 6.3.3 (গ্যাসের প্রসারণ). A glass tank of water stands on a lab bench with two balloons of the same volume (1 L) under the surface, each tied to a small weight on the floor: a rose one filled with air and a blue one filled with water. The student picks how hot the water is (50, 70 or 90 °C) and taps the big button to keep both in the hot water: the balloon of water stays about the same size, the balloon of air swells (its volume follows V = V1 T2/T1 in kelvin, +7, +13 or +20 %; water grows only +1 to +3 %). The picture draws the swelling's radius about 3 times too big, with a dashed ring at the starting size, and says so; the numbers are real. The panel shows both volumes before and after and the book's two sentences (heat does not expand a liquid that much; it expands a gas much more). Three tap questions, one of them using gamma_P = 1/T1 from page 174. The tank, the balloons and the weights export as GLB in metres. Offline, in Bangla and English.
